questions.prompt: The rapid Rhine, swollen with rains, terrified the anxious farmers.
questions.answer: Rhēnus rapidus, imbribus tumidus, agricolās sollicitōs terruit.

questions.prompt: The cold north wind, blowing from the mountains, scattered the sailors' ships.
questions.answer: Aquilō frīgidus, ā montibus flāns, nāvēs nautārum dispersit.

questions.prompt: In April the poet praised the gentle rivers of his homeland.
questions.answer: Aprīlī poēta lēnēs patriae amnēs laudāvit.

questions.prompt: The east wind, to be feared by all, drove the fleet toward Africa.
questions.answer: Eurus, ab omnibus timendus, classem ad Āfricam ēgit.

questions.prompt: The queen, mourning her dead son, gave gifts to the gods.
questions.answer: Rēgīna, mortuum fīlium lūgēns, deīs dōna dedit.

questions.prompt: The farmer's mother, wise and pious, feared the anger of the goddess.
questions.answer: Māter agricolae, sapiēns et pia, īram deae timēbat.

questions.prompt: The sailor, though brave, was weeping at his mother's grave.
questions.answer: Nauta, quamquam fortis, ad mātris sepulcrum flēbat.

questions.prompt: The poet, a famous man, praised the beauty of the maiden.
questions.answer: Poēta, vir clārus, virginis pulchritūdinem laudāvit.

questions.prompt: The divine will punished the impious man's dreadful crime.
questions.answer: Nūmen dīvīnum nefandum hominis facinus pūnīvit.

questions.prompt: The old woman, full of complaints, hated the servant's obedience.
questions.answer: Anus, querēlārum plēna, servī obsequium ōderat.

questions.prompt: Filth and old age had weakened the limbs of the sick king.
questions.answer: Sordēs et vetustās membra rēgis aegrī dēbilitāverant.

questions.prompt: Angry at the poison, the girl mourned her dying brother.
questions.answer: Venēnō īrāta, puella morientem frātrem lūgēbat.

questions.prompt: In March the soldiers crossed the swift Tiber by night.
questions.answer: Mārtiō mīlitēs celerem Tiberim nocte trānsiērunt.

questions.prompt: The warm south wind of summer melted the deep snows.
questions.answer: Auster tepidus aestātis altās nivēs solvit.

questions.prompt: January, harsh with cold, was holding the wide fields in ice.
questions.answer: Iānuārius, frīgore asper, lātōs agrōs glaciē tenēbat.

questions.prompt: The gentle Seine was flowing through the lands of the Gauls.
questions.answer: Sēquana lēnis per Gallōrum terrās fluēbat.

questions.prompt: The king's daughter, betrothed to a god, feared the transformation.
questions.answer: Rēgis fīlia, deō dēstināta, metamorphōsin timēbat.

questions.prompt: The nurse kissed the sleeping boy with tender love.
questions.answer: Nūtrīx dormientem puerum tenerō amōre ōsculāta est.

questions.prompt: Stiff with cold, the aged farmer was cursing the winter winds.
questions.answer: Frīgore rigēns, senex agricola hībernōs ventōs exsecrābātur.

questions.prompt: The messenger announced the success of the war to the anxious queen.
questions.answer: Nūntius bellī successum sollicitae rēgīnae nūntiāvit.

questions.prompt: A small piece of meat delighted the hungry poet.
questions.answer: Parvum copadium ēsurientem poētam dēlectāvit.

questions.prompt: The hidden poison, mixed with wine, killed the greedy king.
questions.answer: Occultum vīrus, vīnō mixtum, avidum rēgem necāvit.

questions.prompt: The winds of November scattered the withered leaves through the streets.
questions.answer: Novembris ventī āridās frondēs per viās sparsērunt.

questions.prompt: The west wind, rising at first light, carried the ships across the sea.
questions.answer: Zephyrus, prīmā lūce surgēns, nāvēs trāns mare portāvit.

questions.prompt: The swift Rhône, deep in winter, carried off the merchant's boats.
questions.answer: Rhodanus rapidus, hieme altus, mercātōris lintrēs abstulit.

questions.prompt: In September the sailors feared the raging south wind.
questions.answer: Mēnse Septembrī nautae Austrum saevientem timēbant.

questions.prompt: The gentle west wind, blowing at first light, was delighting the weary farmer.
questions.answer: Favōnius lēnis, prīmā lūce flāns, agricolam fessum dēlectābat.

questions.prompt: October, harsh with storms, had destroyed the poet's vineyards.
questions.answer: Octōber, tempestātibus asper, poētae vīneās dēlēverat.

questions.prompt: The tall oak, struck by lightning, fell in the sacred grove.
questions.answer: Quercus alta, fulmine icta, in lūcō sacrō cecidit.

questions.prompt: Ancient Corinth, famous for its wealth, was destroyed by the Romans.
questions.answer: Corinthus antīqua, dīvitiīs clāra, ā Rōmānīs dēlēta est.

questions.prompt: Rhodes, dear to sailors, nourishes many olive trees.
questions.answer: Rhodus, nautīs cāra, multās olīvās alit.

questions.prompt: The wide-spreading beech gave shade to the resting shepherd.
questions.answer: Fāgus lāta pāstōrī quiēscentī umbram praebēbat.

questions.prompt: The trustworthy scribe, sitting in the forum, wrote the general's letters.
questions.answer: Scrība fidēlis, in forō sedēns, ducis epistulās scrīpsit.

questions.prompt: The bold pirate, to be feared throughout the whole sea, seized the rich merchant.
questions.answer: Pīrāta audāx, tōtō marī metuendus, mercātōrem dīvitem cēpit.

questions.prompt: The diligent farmer, though weary, praised his devoted daughter.
questions.answer: Agricola dīligēns, quamquam fessus, fīliam piam laudāvit.

questions.prompt: The famous poet, crowned with laurel, sang of the ancient kings.
questions.answer: Poēta clārus, laurō corōnātus, dē rēgibus antīquīs cecinit.

questions.prompt: The holy and revered priestess guarded the sacred flame by night.
questions.answer: Sacerdōs sāncta ac veneranda flammam sacram nocte custōdiēbat.

questions.prompt: Every citizen, mindful of the laws, obeyed the just consul.
questions.answer: Cīvis omnis, lēgum memor, cōnsulī iūstō pārēbat.

questions.prompt: The anxious parent, worn out by cares, watched over the sleeping infant.
questions.answer: Parēns sollicitus, cūrīs cōnfectus, īnfantem dormientem cūrābat.

questions.prompt: The aged priest, standing at the altar, sacrificed a white bull to Jupiter.
questions.answer: Sacerdōs senex, ad āram stāns, taurum album Iovī immolāvit.

questions.prompt: To conquer oneself is difficult, but pleasing to the gods.
questions.answer: Sē vincere difficile est, sed deīs grātum.

questions.prompt: Nothing is more precious than uncorrupted virtue.
questions.answer: Nihil est pretiōsius quam virtūs incorrupta.

questions.prompt: To have lived well is a great reward for the wise man.
questions.answer: Bene vīxisse magnum praemium sapientī est.

questions.prompt: It is wrong to betray one's country to the enemy.
questions.answer: Nefās est patriam hostibus prōdere.

questions.prompt: The cunning fox, lurking in the woods, snatched the farmer's goose.
questions.answer: Vulpēs callida, in silvīs latēns, agricolae ānserem rapuit.

questions.prompt: The swift eagle, sacred to Jupiter, seized the trembling hare.
questions.answer: Aquila celeris, Iovī sacra, leporem trepidantem rapuit.

questions.prompt: The savage wolf, driven by hunger, wandered through the snowy fields.
questions.answer: Lupus saevus, famē āctus, per campōs nivōsōs errābat.

questions.prompt: The white swan, gliding on the calm water, sang a sweet song.
questions.answer: Cygnus albus, in aquā tranquillā lābēns, dulce carmen cecinit.
